newsitem.title: SPAIN: Spain denies corruption allegations against Aznar.
newsitem.headline: Spain denies corruption allegations against Aznar.

text.p: Spain's government denied on Friday that Prime Minister Jose Maria Aznar had received illegal kickbacks to fund a regional electoral campaign.

In the first public accusation of corruption since Aznar came to power, a Spanish newspaper published a court document on Thursday in which a businessman accused the prime minister of receiving money in exchange for awarding construction contracts.

"The accusations are absolutely false," government spokesman Miguel Angel Rodriguez told reporters after the weekly cabinet meeting. "The Popular Party will be presenting a criminal charge for defamation."

During his electoral bid, Aznar campaigned on a clean-hands platform against the former Socialist government, which had been discredited by a series of corruption scandals during its 13 years in power.

But businessman Eduardo Corrales accused Aznar of taking 3.0 million pesetas ($21,000) from two construction firms in 1987 when he was head of the Popular Alliance, a party which later became the Popular Party (PP) in the Castille-Leon region.
Corrales claimed the funds had been channelled into Aznar's electoral bid for the region, which he subsequently won.
In addition, Corrales said he himself had handed over 12.5 million pesetas ($87,000) in a two-and-a-half-year period to the PP in the Zamora region, in exchange for contracts.
Corrales, who knew the prime minister from his days as Castille-Leon head, wrote Aznar a letter demanding that he clean up his party.
